answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each identity must continuously publish verifiable work traces; admission to tasks requires an unbroken tundra-length history of such traces. Validation samples past intervals at random, so a fresh identity costs the full sustained-attention span before it can act. An attacker must run every sybil through that same voyage of continuous, checkable output. Publishing a coherent sonnet-grade trace per interval multiplies the cost linearly per identity.
